phases.name: 问题清单
phases.instructions:
Start from the current user request and any resumed conversation or explicit workflow carryover. Then, when available, use project-context.md and run-report.md as supporting notes before updating debug-context.md and debug-work-order.md with every user-requested item before investigation. Do not silently choose only the first symptom. For each debug task record a stable id, symptom, expected/actual behavior, evidence and logs, reproduction clues, affected area, suspected relationship to other tasks, accepted/deferred decision, priority, dependencies, target files and write scopes, and validation cases.

Ask the user only when a missing user-specific fact blocks the current phase after checking the request, workspace, logs, and workflow artifacts. If you ask, set blocksCompletion true and provide blockingReason and answerImpact. After an answer, carry it into current-phase work before phase completion. Ask a further question only when, after considering that answer and the workspace, a distinct user-specific fact still blocks the current phase; otherwise choose and record a conservative default.

For each accepted symptom, record the expected behavior, actual behavior, evidence already available, and the concrete observation that would show the issue is resolved. If a user answer is needed, link it to that reproduction or acceptance decision instead of collecting it as a standalone questionnaire response.

Inherited context and workspace grounding:
- Treat the current user request plus any resumed conversation or explicit workflow carryover as the primary context. Read project-context.md and run-report.md as supporting workflow notes, not as a replacement for the current request; if either is absent, stale, or conflicts with the current request, record and update the discrepancy.
- Before asking a question, use read-only discovery: Glob for the smallest relevant file surface, Grep for relevant symbols or log entries, and Read for targeted contents. Use LS only when the host exposes it; never fall back to Bash or PowerShell merely to list or search files. Inspect user-named paths, immediate manifests or entry points, supplied error logs, and the relevant symptom surface. Record a small project map: workspace root, user-specified target, suspected areas, evidence locations, and important unknowns.
- Do not blindly scan an entire repository. Inspect only the smallest project surface needed to inventory every reported debug task and begin reproducible investigation.

### Focused problem clarification and first evidence pass

Build an inventory for every reported problem before repair. Start with the request, source, existing AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, workflow context, application logs, error reports, and reproducible evidence. For each task capture the observed symptom, expected behavior, trigger/reproduction context, impact, environment/version, available diagnostics, constraints, and user-visible acceptance outcome.

After that first evidence pass, create a diagnostic decision coverage checklist for every accepted symptom. Evaluate: exact expected contract, reproduction/frequency and affected boundary, environment/version/data conditions, user impact and priority, compatibility or recovery behavior, allowed side effects, rollback/containment needs, and the observable acceptance proof. A plausible code-level root cause does not settle an intended behavior or repair-policy choice that is absent from code and evidence.

When one or more material diagnostic or repair-policy decisions remain unknown, ask one structured AskUserQuestion before repair. Ask exactly one unresolved material diagnostic or repair-policy decision at a time, state the evidence already known, offer bounded choices when useful, and give answerImpact. Incorporate the answer into diagnosis and repair planning, then explicitly reassess the existing diagnostic decision coverage checklist. If another independent material decision in that checklist remains unresolved, ask it in the next AskUserQuestion call. Continue sequentially until every material diagnostic or repair-policy decision in that existing checklist is settled; thorough clarification is encouraged, but never combine several questions in one call. Do not require a complete preflight questionnaire before investigation or repair can proceed.

Maintain a clarification ledger in debug-context.md and debug-work-order.md: question id, settled answer or evidence, affected debug task ids, diagnosis/repair impact, and explicit deferments. Do not ask for status confirmation, duplicate a logged symptom, or ask the user to repeat information already available in code/logs/workflow context. Before a later question, consult that ledger and the current conversation; ask again only when new evidence conflicts with a recorded answer or exposes a distinct material decision.

For a genuinely non-material gap, state a bounded hypothesis and the lowest-cost discriminating check, record it, and begin investigation.

### Multi-symptom focused clarification

When a request reports more than one user-visible symptom, first use the available code and logs to separate what is already evidenced from what remains genuinely unknown. Before creating the authoritative debug-context.md or debug-work-order.md, ask exactly one focused question only when one unresolved decision about terminal behavior, validation/input handling, affected data or accounts, recovery/rollback, or user-visible acceptance would materially change the repair. Incorporate the answer before asking a distinct follow-up. Do not silently choose a material policy, but do not combine several questions in one AskUserQuestion call or turn a multi-symptom report into a progress questionnaire. For a material gap that cannot be safely bounded, keep blocksCompletion true until its single answer is incorporated.

### Soft project continuity context
Before asking the user or changing code, inspect the smallest relevant portions of existing AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .workflow/project-context.md, .workflow/work-order.md, and documented application logs. These are optional sources, not required project structure: if they are absent, stale, inaccessible, or unrelated, record that limitation and continue from the request and observable code.

When an accepted task changes architecture, commands, behavior contracts, diagnostics, data handling, or maintenance guidance, update the relevant existing AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. Do not overwrite unrelated instructions. If no such files exist, do not block the work or fabricate them; mention a concise optional maintenance recommendation only when it would materially help future work.

### Debug Capsule

Maintain these fixed fields for every accepted symptom: 用户现象, 复现步骤, 日志证据, 已验证事实, 假设, 已排除原因, 根本原因, 修复, 回归证据. Start from the user report, then proactively inspect relevant existing logs and code; do not ask the user to repeat evidence already available. AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and application logs are optional sources, not prerequisites.

phases.name: 问题排查
phases.instructions:
For every accepted task in debug-work-order.md, reproduce the symptom or document a credible could-not-reproduce path, then identify root cause, impact, and minimal fix strategy. First assess dependencies, overlapping target files and write scopes, shared resources, and whether evidence supports a shared root cause. Build a workflow_parallel_plan only for logically isolated investigation batches; do not impose a numeric concurrency cap. The host scheduler decides feasible parallelism from dependencies, write scopes, and resource claims. Do not complete investigation while any accepted task lacks reproduction/could-not-reproduce evidence and a planned terminal path.

Ask the user only when a missing user-specific fact blocks the current phase after checking the request, workspace, logs, and workflow artifacts. If you ask, set blocksCompletion true and provide blockingReason and answerImpact. After an answer, carry it into current-phase work before phase completion. Ask a further question only when, after considering that answer and the workspace, a distinct user-specific fact still blocks the current phase; otherwise choose and record a conservative default.

Use a lightweight diagnosis loop for every accepted task: record the current hypothesis, the discriminating check, the observed result, and the planned terminal path. Do not ask for a progress confirmation when code, logs, workspace evidence, or a conservative reproduction path can move the investigation forward.

### Investigate without progress prompts

Continue from the accepted inventory, consolidated answers, and first-pass evidence. Do not ask whether to proceed to the next bug, whether to run the planned investigation, or whether to inspect available logs. Use logs and project guidance when present; distinguish observed evidence from hypotheses. Ask only when investigation reaches a genuine user-specific blocker that code, tests, logs, and a bounded conservative path cannot resolve.

### Soft project continuity context
Before asking the user or changing code, inspect the smallest relevant portions of existing AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .workflow/project-context.md, .workflow/work-order.md, and documented application logs. These are optional sources, not required project structure: if they are absent, stale, inaccessible, or unrelated, record that limitation and continue from the request and observable code.

When an accepted task changes architecture, commands, behavior contracts, diagnostics, data handling, or maintenance guidance, update the relevant existing AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. Do not overwrite unrelated instructions. If no such files exist, do not block the work or fabricate them; mention a concise optional maintenance recommendation only when it would materially help future work.

### Mandatory pre-coding parallelization plan

Before completing this planning phase, create an internal repairParallelizationPlan in debug-work-order.md. This is technical execution planning, not a user-facing confirmation: do not ask the user whether to parallelize.

Assess the complete remaining implementation set, not only the next task. For every candidate coding or repair batch, record: batch/task IDs and goal; prerequisite IDs and the concrete evidence that each prerequisite is already stable or completed; exact expected writeScopes at file or narrow directory level; shared resourceClaims such as schema, API contract, shared state, build configuration, generated output, test fixture, or environment ownership; independent validation; worktree/isolation requirement for write work; and the decision `parallel group <wave>` or `serial`, with a concrete reason.

A completed predecessor is not a concurrent write conflict. A shared parent module or broad directory name is not enough to force serial work: identify the actual overlapping file, mutable resource, unstable contract, or dependency. Conversely, never invent parallelism merely to increase agent count. A serial-only plan is valid only when every remaining candidate has a recorded concrete conflict or dependency.

Use the plan to form safe waves: all batches in one `parallel group <wave>` must have satisfied prerequisites, isolated non-overlapping writeScopes and resourceClaims, independent validation, and an available isolated worktree for write execution. Within each batch, Coder -> Reviewer -> bounded Coder fixes -> Reviewer remains strictly serial. At the coding phase, re-check this plan against the actual current tree before delegation; launch every still-safe independent wave in parallel through workflow_parallel_plan, and revise only when fresh code evidence changes the recorded dependency or conflict.

For Debug, distinguish read-only investigation parallelism from later write repair parallelism. Do not launch Coder work in this investigation phase. The repairParallelizationPlan must cover only tasks with a confirmed or bounded repair path and be carried into debug-fix for its final current-tree re-check.

### Diagnostic Evidence Discipline (mandatory)
For every accepted symptom, record whether application logs are used, not-applicable, or unavailable. Do not force logs for a pure visual/layout problem when logs cannot prove the symptom; record not-applicable with the reason. When logs are used, record the concrete paths, failure-time window, search terms or observations, and what they do or do not establish. When logs are unavailable, record the locations checked and the reason. Code inspection alone must be identified as code evidence, not runtime evidence.


### One-question workflow clarification contract
Ask only one necessary user question in each AskUserQuestion call. Continue with another one-question card only when, after incorporating the prior answer and current evidence, a distinct unresolved user-specific fact still blocks a correct decision. Do not repeat answered facts, do not bundle unrelated decisions into a packet, and do not require an artifact or phase completion between independent necessary questions. A business answer is not a workflow route: collect the answer first, then use submit_phase_completion or request_workflow_route only when their separate conditions are actually met.

### Executable batch-parallelism contract
Before coding or repair, examine the complete remaining batch set using real dependency edges, write scopes, shared resources, and validation dependencies. Conclude serial execution when the evidence shows a dependency or conflict; do not choose serial merely to avoid analysis. Only truly isolated batches may run in parallel. For every qualifying parallel wave, call Agent once per assigned task with non-empty description and prompt, subagent_type=general-purpose, the matching top-level workflow_role, and the same complete workflow_parallel_plan object on every call:
- workflow_parallel_plan.task_id is the assigned task id for that Agent call.
- workflow_parallel_plan.tasks contains every task in the active phase, each with id, depends_on, write_scopes, resource_claims, and execution_mode.
- Use asynchronous execution: set run_in_background=true when that field is visible. If the runtime hides it for fork mode, do not invent the field; the host executes the worker asynchronously.
Within one batch, Coder → Reviewer → bounded Coder repair → Reviewer is strictly serial. Parallelism is only between separate batches after their Coder/Reviewer chains have been proven isolated.

### Debug Capsule evidence update

For every accepted symptom, inspect relevant existing logs proactively when available, then update 日志证据, 已验证事实, 假设, 已排除原因, and 根本原因. Do not repeat an excluded hypothesis unless new evidence invalidates the earlier exclusion. Missing logs do not block investigation; record unavailable or not-applicable with a reason.

Never silently omit a remaining accepted task; record an explicit user deferral or blocker instead.

phases.instructions:
Run regression checks and scenario validation for every accepted task in debug-work-order.md, including cross-task regressions when tasks interact. A missing accepted-task result blocks completion. If validation finds a code defect, call request_workflow_route with targetPhaseId debug-fix, preserve the failure evidence, and wait for debug-fix to repair and re-review it. Do not code or repair in this quality phase. Use preview controls when useful or document why preview was skipped.

Ask the user only when a missing user-specific fact blocks the current phase after checking the request, workspace, logs, and workflow artifacts. If you ask, set blocksCompletion true and provide blockingReason and answerImpact. After an answer, carry it into current-phase work before phase completion. Ask a further question only when, after considering that answer and the workspace, a distinct user-specific fact still blocks the current phase; otherwise choose and record a conservative default.

Treat this as outcome review, not only command review: compare the observed behavior with the original expected/actual symptom and record the regression result, any remaining mismatch, and the next scoped repair or user decision. Do not ask the user to confirm progress when the scenario can be checked from the workspace or existing evidence.

### Compact regression closeout

Treat regression checking, preview evidence, and the route-back handoff as one closeout path. Do not ask the user to authorize ordinary regression work or phase progress. Only surface a question when the observed result requires a product decision, cannot be reproduced safely, or reveals an unresolved risk outside the accepted repair scope.

### Soft project continuity context
Before asking the user or changing code, inspect the smallest relevant portions of existing AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .workflow/project-context.md, .workflow/work-order.md, and documented application logs. If no such files exist, do not block the work or fabricate them; mention a concise optional maintenance recommendation only when it would materially help future work.

### Debug Core-Flow Evidence and Honest Runtime Status (mandatory)
Write .workflow/runs/<runId>/core-flow-evidence.json with schemaVersion 1 and one flows entry for every accepted symptom. Each entry must include coreFlowId, entryBoundary, expectedCheckpoints, observedCheckpoints, logEvidence, and execution.

logEvidence must be exactly one of: used { paths, timeWindow, observations }, not-applicable { reason }, or unavailable { reason }. execution must declare status pass|partial|not-run and method runtime|manual-preview|integration|static. A pass requires non-static execution, observed checkpoints, and a visible result. A partial/not-run path requires nextAction.

After repair and Reviewer pass, return and rerun the affected scenario. Retry, tool failure, or Agent completion must not advance the phase.

intent.objective: Finish the bug fix while preserving reproducible evidence and project memory.

contract.instructions:
Update project memory and run report, then close the debug workflow or prepare a confirmed follow-up workflow.

### Non-blocking debug archive

This is a durable evidence archive, not a new clarification stage. Use the accepted task inventory, diagnosis, fix log, regression evidence, and relevant existing guidance/logs to produce the handoff. Do not reopen routine questions; record explicit residual uncertainty or a concrete follow-up only when it remains.

### Soft project continuity context
Before asking the user or changing code, inspect the smallest relevant portions of existing AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .workflow/project-context.md, .workflow/work-order.md, and documented application logs. These are optional sources, not required project structure: if they are absent, stale, inaccessible, or unrelated, record that limitation and continue from the request and observable code.

When an accepted task changes architecture, commands, behavior contracts, diagnostics, data handling, or maintenance guidance, update the relevant existing AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. Do not overwrite unrelated instructions. If no such files exist, do not block the work or fabricate them; mention a concise optional maintenance recommendation only when it would materially help future work.
